56		keysSorted := make([]string, 0, len(groups))
57		for key := range groups {
58			keysSorted = append(keysSorted, key)
59		}
60		sort.Strings(keysSorted)
61		for _, key := range keysSorted {
62			sides := groups[key]
63			present := make(map[string]struct{})
64			for _, side := range sides {
65				for p := range side {
66					present[p] = struct{}{}
67				}
68			}
69			if len(present) <= 1 || isCaseOnlyRename(manifest, scans, sides) {
70				continue
71			}
72			names := make([]string, 0, len(present))
73			for p := range present {
74				names = append(names, p)
75			}
76			sort.Strings(names)
77			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q and %q; give these paths distinct names, or the same spelling on both sides, before syncing", ErrCaseAlias, names[0], names[1])
78		}
79		return nil
80	}
81	
82	func keys(files map[string]FileEntry) map[string]struct{} {
83		out := make(map[string]struct{}, len(files))
84		for p := range files {
85			out[p] = struct{}{}
86		}
87		return out
88	}
89	
90	// isCaseOnlyRename recognizes a file renamed by case on one side only: each
91	// side holds exactly one spelling, they differ only in the last component,
92	// the old spelling is the tracked one, and its holder still has exactly the
93	// tracked content. The planner then deletes the unchanged old spelling and
94	// creates the new one; the executor's exclusive publish and observed-entry
95	// checks keep those two actions from touching one file through two names,
96	// so on a case-insensitive side the create simply waits a cycle.
97	//
98	// Content is compared by hash, so the fast (size+mtime) path, whose
99	// baseline carries no hashes, never qualifies: its executor overwrites and
100	// deletes without those checks.
101	func isCaseOnlyRename(manifest map[string]db.ManifestRow, scans []ScanResult, sides []map[string]struct{}) bool {
102		if len(scans) != 2 || len(sides[0]) != 1 || len(sides[1]) != 1 {
103			return false
104		}
105		var spelled [2]string
106		for i, side := range sides {
107			for p := range side {
108				spelled[i] = p
109			}
110		}
111		if spelled[0] == spelled[1] || path.Dir(spelled[0]) != path.Dir(spelled[1]) {
112			return false
113		}
114		_, tracked0 := manifest[spelled[0]]
115		_, tracked1 := manifest[spelled[1]]
116		if tracked0 == tracked1 {
117			return false
118		}
119		oldSide := 0
120		if tracked1 {
121			oldSide = 1
122		}
123		old, renamed := spelled[oldSide], spelled[1-oldSide]
124		row := manifest[old]
125		entry, ok := scans[oldSide].Files[old]
126		if !ok || row.Hash == "" || entry.Hash != row.Hash || entry.Size != row.Size {
127			return false
128		}
129		_, isFile := scans[1-oldSide].Files[renamed]
130		return isFile
131	}
132	
133	// CheckScopedCaseAliases inspects names in affected parent directories
134	// without scanning or hashing their unrelated files. It cannot tell a
135	// case-only rename from a genuine collision; RunRobustScoped answers an
136	// ErrCaseAlias from it with a full cycle, whose CheckCaseAliases can.
137	//
138	// The baseline is deliberately not consulted: listing each affected parent
139	// on both sides already sees every spelling that exists there, and a
140	// baseline spelling that exists on neither side is a stale row the planner
141	// only drops (see CheckCaseAliases). Loading the whole manifest here made
142	// every fsnotify batch cost as much as the tree.
143	func CheckScopedCaseAliases(local, remote *Tree, paths map[string]struct{}, scopes ...ScanResult) error {
144		fold := cases.Fold()
145		targets := map[string]map[string]string{}
146		add := func(rel string) {
147			for ; rel != "." && rel != "/"; rel = path.Dir(rel) {
148				parent, name := path.Dir(rel), path.Base(rel)
149				if targets[parent] == nil {
150					targets[parent] = map[string]string{}
151				}
152				targets[parent][fold.String(name)] = name
153			}
154		}
155		for rel := range paths {
156			add(rel)
157		}
158		for _, scope := range scopes {
159			for rel := range scope.Files {
160				add(rel)
161			}
162			for rel := range scope.Dirs {
163				add(rel)
164			}
165		}
166		check := func(parent, actual string) error {
167			actual = norm.NFC.String(actual)
168			if wanted, ok := targets[parent][fold.String(actual)]; ok && wanted != actual {
169				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %q and %q", ErrCaseAlias, path.Join(parent, wanted), path.Join(parent, actual))
170			}
171			return nil
172		}
173		for _, tree := range []*Tree{local, remote} {
174			for parent := range targets {
175				dir, err := tree.directory(filepath.FromSlash(parent), 0)
176				if os.IsNotExist(err) || errors.Is(err, ErrSymlink) {
177					continue
178				}
179				if err != nil {
180					return err
181				}
182				names, err := dir.Readdirnames(-1)
183				dir.Close()
184				if err != nil {
185					return err
186				}
187				for _, actual := range names {
188					// Another syncd's in-flight (or retained) entry: reported
189					// by the scanner, never reconciled.
190					if strings.HasPrefix(actual, holdingPrefix) {
191						continue
192					}
193					if err := check(parent, actual); err != nil {
194						return err
195					}
196				}
197			}
198		}
199		return nil
200	}
201

content.text:
I've made the deploy script wait for each restarted daemon's first full cycle. It needed a small syncd change first, because the daemon had no way to say when that cycle finished. The checks are green (build, vet, tests, race, both cross-compiles), but nothing is committed yet. I also haven't run the wait end to end: the daemons running now don't log the new line, so it only works once a new binary is deployed.

**syncd change** (branch `feat/log-first-full-cycle`): [loop.go](internal/watch/loop.go) now logs `watch: first full cycle complete` once per run, after the first whole-tree cycle that succeeds. It isn't logged if the canary check fails, the delete limit refuses the cycle, or the cycle errors. A new test, `TestRunLogsFirstFullCycleOnce`, covers both the case where it's logged once and the case where it isn't logged at all.

**`~/deploy-syncd.sh`:**
- **What it waits on:** after each restart it reads the service's own flags (from the launchd plist on the Mac, from systemd's ExecStart on Linux). From those it finds the log, the local root and the `--remote-poll` interval.
- **How it judges success:** it looks only at log lines written after the restart. It succeeds when the new process logs the line above, and fails at once if the new process logs an error first.
- **Timeout:** the poll interval plus 300s, changeable with `SYNCD_WAIT_TIMEOUT`. When it times out, it says whether the daemon never started (for example, still waiting for the share to mount) or started but didn't finish a cycle.
- **Mac and Linux run in parallel:** the Mac wait runs in the background while the Linux host does its install and wait, so the total is about one poll interval rather than two.
- **Exit status and opt-out:** the script exits non-zero if any daemon fails to finish its first cycle. `--no-wait` skips the waiting.

I ran the wait logic against made-up logs, including an old run's errors, a restart, an error after the restart, and a missing log. I also checked that the service flags are read correctly on both machines.

When you're ready, I can commit, open a PR, merge it, and then deploy from `main` to try the wait on both machines.

content.text:
It's shipped and deployed. The deploy script now waited for both daemons to finish their first full cycle, and both did. The whole deploy, tests included, took about 70 seconds.

- **PR:** [william-coronado/syncd#8](https://github.com/william-coronado/syncd/pull/8) is merged into `main` with a merge commit. The branch is deleted on GitHub and here.
- **Deploy:** `~/deploy-syncd.sh --test` installed the new binary from `main` on both machines and restarted both services. The Linux daemon finished its first full cycle, then the Mac daemon did, and the script exited cleanly.

**About the `-p` folder:** I created it by mistake. During the SMB testing earlier I ran `mkdir "$P/raw" -p` from inside the repo. macOS `mkdir` doesn't treat `-p` as an option when it comes after the folder name, so it created an empty folder called `-p` in the repo. The watch daemon then copied it to the share and to the Linux host. It was empty and never committed. I've removed all three copies with `rmdir`, which only deletes empty folders.
